summary: TypeScript streaming reconnect results in duplicated external tool invocations when SDK retries
description:
Issue summary: Customer LexaHealth reports repeated invocations of an external webhook/tool when using our TypeScript SDK streaming API. The app uses function-calling (tool invocation) to run side effects; after a transient network blip the SDK reconnects and appears to replay the tool call, causing duplicate downstream actions (duplicate patient notifications).

Impact: Production impact for a single customer — duplicate notifications sent to end users. Potential regulatory sensitivity for health-related notifications. Happened intermittently across several requests; not a full outage but high customer impact.

Environment: Redwood TS SDK v1.5.3, Node 18, prod region us-east, using dedicated capacity (customer-managed routing rules). Tool call performed via function-calling API with a customer webhook target.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Start a streaming chat session with function-calling enabled and provide an idempotency token only on the top-level request (not on the function call payload).
2. Trigger an input that results in a function call by the model (tool name: notify_patient).
3. Simulate a transient disconnect (customer reported a brief WebSocket disconnect at ~300ms into response). SDK auto-reconnects and resumes.
4. Observe two outbound POSTs to the customer's webhook within ~1s of each other.

Expected: Single invocation of notify_patient per model decision. SDK should avoid replaying tool calls after reconnect unless the model explicitly re-issues them.

Actual: The SDK's reconnect path replays the last tool invocation payload to the server which results in the serving runtime invoking the tool again. This appears correlated with streaming reconnect + SDK-side retry/backoff interaction.

Logs (customer-provided):
- SDK client reconnect record: "ws disconnect code=1006, reconnecting, attempt=1"
- Outbound webhook traces: POST /webhooks/notify_patient 2026-03-10T14:22:31.102Z -> 2026-03-10T14:22:31.453Z and POST 2026-03-10T14:22:31.712Z
- SDK request id: req-lexa-9a7f

Additional notes: Customer does not pass an explicit idempotency-key for function invocation (they rely on top-level request id). They use the TypeScript SDK streaming convenience which hides some of the low-level frames. They are on a dedicated pool that has routing fallback enabled.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Elena Park (Support): Created ticket after initial customer report. Asked for full SDK debug logs, the raw WS frames and the webhook headers. Requested reproduction script.

2026-03-10 16:10 - LexaHealth (Customer): Provided logs and a minimal repro snippet using SDK v1.5.3. Confirmed duplicate webhooks only appear when network blip is introduced. Asked for urgent mitigation; duplicated notifications affect patient workflow.

2026-03-11 09:22 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Initial triage. Reproduced locally with the repro script when forcing a socket close mid-stream. Observed the client resend of the last 'function_call' frame on reconnect. Hypothesis: client-side reconnect logic resends unacknowledged frames and the serving-runtime treats function_call frames as new actions rather than de-duplicating based on request-level idempotency.

2026-03-11 11:05 - Anya Gomez (SDK Lead): Noted that TypeScript SDK currently attaches idempotency-key at top-level request but does not propagate it into the function-call meta. Suggested workaround: customer to set a function-level idempotency header or include an idempotent identifier in the function payload. Also flagged need for SDK change: mark function_call frames as non-replayable or attach persistent idempotency token to sub-ops.

2026-03-11 13:40 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Confirmed serving-runtime accepts function_call frames as independent decisions and executes tool routing immediately. Filing companion PR to add short-term server-side dedupe for repeated identical function_call payloads within a 2s sliding window per request id. Linked PR github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/289.

2026-03-12 08:17 - Support (Elena): Sent mitigation steps to LexaHealth: (1) Add a function-level idempotency token in the function payload (suggested key: lexahid). (2) Update SDK usage to enable "suppressReplayOnReconnect" flag (temporary internal flag available in v1.5.4-beta). Customer requested timeline for stable fix.

2026-03-12 10:00 - LexaHealth (Customer): Implemented function-level idempotency and reports no duplicate notifications in two hours of synthetic load. Requests a request for permanent SDK fix and a postmortem style note.

2026-03-12 14:05 - Anya Gomez (SDK Lead): Assigned SDK work to handle function_call idempotency propagation. Plan: (A) Ensure SDK attaches sub-operation id to function_call frames and preserves it across reconnects, (B) Add opt-in client flag to never replay function_call frames on reconnect, (C) Document recommended patterns. Target stable release v1.6.0. Marking ticket In Progress.
investigation_notes: Client behavior: TS SDK 1.5.3 queues outgoing frames and on reconnect re-emits any frame not acked by server. No special-case for function_call frames.

Server behavior: serving-runtime executes function_call frames idempotently only at request boundary; no sub-operation dedupe currently. We observed two executions with identical payload & signature within the same request id.

Hypothesis: combination of streaming reconnect + lack of sub-operation idempotency results in duplicate tool execution. Deduping on server-side by payload signature within a small window reduces duplicates but does not address root SDK ergonomics.
Risk assessment: Medium - happens only when stream reconnects mid-response. For high-volume customers or those with side-effectful tools this is high impact.
workaround: Customer implemented function-level idempotency token in the function payload and saw immediate mitigation. Short-term server-side dedupe PR created (see related PR). Recommend customer keep the token until SDK v1.6.0 is released.
next_steps: Merge server-side sliding-window dedupe (PR #289) and deploy to staging for canary testing.
Implement SDK change to propagate sub-operation id and opt-out replay flag; include tests for reconnect scenarios.
Create an SDK docs guide for "Function-calling & idempotency" with code examples for TS/Python/Go.
Prepare a short post-incident note for LexaHealth outlining root cause, mitigation, and timeline for permanent fix.
